newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rebuffs U.S. over Syrian arms row.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rebuffs U.S. over Syrian arms row.

text.p: U.S. condemnation of a proposed South African arms sale to Syria is unacceptable grandstanding and Pretoria will not be dictated to by Washington, a spokesman for President Nelson Mandela said on Tuesday.
Spokesman Parks Mankahlana was responding to a U.S. threat to cut aid to South Africa if it went ahead with the proposed sale of tank fire control systems to Syria.
"We detest this kind of behaviour," Mankahlana told Reuters.
"We don't like grandstanding and they should not do that... They are not going to guide us, they are not going to tell us what to do," he said.

The United States said it was deeply concerned about the proposed sale and warned South Africa that under U.S. law it would have no option but to cut off aid if South Africa sold weapons to a country considered a "state sponsor of terrorism".
